# Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2019 Summary

The Liberal Democrats present a vision for a "fair, free and open society" centered on fundamental values of liberty, equality, and community. Their central pledge is to **stop Brexit and remain in the EU**, which they argue would secure a £50 billion "Remain Bonus" to invest in public services.

## Key Policy Areas

**Economy:** The party proposes £130 billion in infrastructure investment, a new Skills Wallet giving every adult £10,000 for education and training, and raising R&D spending to 3% of GDP. They advocate for regional rebalancing through a £50 billion programme, while committing to responsible fiscal management and a new wellbeing-focused approach to budgeting.

**Climate Emergency:** Their most urgent domestic priority, proposing an emergency ten-year programme to cut greenhouse gas emissions to net-zero by 2045. Key commitments include 80% renewable electricity by 2030, insulating all homes by 2030, ending fuel poverty by 2025, banning fracking, and planting 60 million trees annually.

**Education:** The manifesto promises free childcare from nine months for working parents, reversing school funding cuts with 20,000 additional teachers, scrapping mandatory SATs, and introducing broader curriculum measures including a "curriculum for life."

**Health and Social Care:** A 1p Income Tax rise would raise £7 billion annually, ringfenced for NHS and social care. Mental health receives special emphasis, with pledges to achieve genuine parity with physical health through £11 billion in additional investment.

**Social Justice:** Proposals include reforming Universal Credit, reducing the first payment wait from five weeks to five days, building 100,000 social homes annually, and ending rough sleeping within five years.

**Civil Liberties and Immigration:** The party commits to defending the Human Rights Act, scrapping the hostile environment, introducing a 28-day immigration detention limit, and giving asylum seekers the right to work after three months.

**Democratic Reform:** Proposals include introducing proportional representation, votes at 16, reforming the House of Lords, and pursuing a federal UK with a written constitution.

**International Affairs:** The manifesto commits to 0.7% GNI on aid, strengthening NATO, maintaining nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament, and championing human rights globally.

Throughout, the Liberal Democrats position themselves as the progressive, forward-looking alternative to what they characterise as backwards-looking Labour and Conservative parties, emphasizing evidence-based policy and international cooperation.
